Why it is built this way

THE OPPOSITE OF VERDANT (owner, 2026-09-17). Verdant names a cover and spreads it; this names one that takes cover away. It reuses the same 'spread' verb and the same radius, chance and interval that verdant's three covers use, so the two genes behave identically except in what the translator does with the word - which is the whole point of the verb taking a vocabulary word rather than a block id.

WHAT IT WILL NOT EAT. The translator converts grass, moss, mycelium and podzol to dirt, and kills wild growth standing on the ground. It deliberately leaves crops, saplings, potted plants and anything else a player put there alone, for the same reason 'melt' leaves packed and blue ice alone: a gene that eats somebody's wheat field is griefing with extra steps. That judgement lives on the game side with the code that knows the blocks.

RECESSIVE, AND SEEDED AS THE EXPRESSING PAIR. The founder table seeds Bli/Bli directly rather than seeding carriers and letting Hardy-Weinberg produce the homozygote, which is what 'flying' does and for the same reason: at any frequency low enough to be rare, p-squared rounds to no wild horse ever having it. About one wild horse in three hundred blights the ground; nothing carries it invisibly.

IT PAINTS NOTHING, so it has no layers and no icon of its own, exactly like verdant. A blighting horse looks like any other horse until you follow it.

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Blight

Ground cover dies back from the hooves. Grass blocks, moss, mycelium and podzol all revert to plain dirt, and wild growth standing on them - grass, ferns and flowers - withers away. Nothing a player planted or placed is touched.

Paints nothing.
